title: Blancism
author: V.I. Lenin
context: Published in Pravda No. 27 on April 8 (21), 1917, shortly after Lenin's return to Petrograd and the presentation of his April Theses, this article exposes the Menshevik and Socialist-Revolutionary leadership of the Soviets for repeating the tragic class-collaborationist illusions of the French reformist Louis Blanc in 1848.
relatesToToday: Critically relevant for dissecting social-democratic and centrist politicians who attempt to manage imperialist capitalist states, make cosmetic anti-war declarations, and sow illusions that capitalist governments can be lobbied into peaceful anti-imperialism.
keyTakeaways: Blancism denotes substituting petty-bourgeois reformist illusions and class collaboration for militant proletarian class struggle.
The Menshevik and SR conciliators in the Soviets repeated Louis Blanc's 1848 error by looking to the capitalist Provisional Government to organize society in the interests of labor.
Petty-bourgeois politicians condemn imperialism in words while demanding that the bourgeoisie renounce annexations without overthrowing the world capitalist system.
Anti-imperialist rhetoric remains an empty deception unless backed by concrete deeds and the revolutionary overthrow of finance capital.
